title: "Overview"
date: last-modified
description: "What this book runs on the Suppinger gastruloids, and where the theory lives."
---

This book applies DeCovarT to the Suppinger murine gastruloid resource.
It records what is run: the data, the algorithms as implemented, the
hyperparameters and their values, the code, the outputs, and which
outputs are stale. The reasons behind each choice are in the DeCovarT
vignettes; each chapter links to the vignette section that states them
and does not restate the theory.

## Aims {#sec-aims}

1. Estimate, for each labelled cell type $j$ at each bulk-matched time,
   the mean $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}$ and the within-type
   covariance $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{W,j}$ of a gene panel, on
   the linear scale that DeCovarT's convolution needs. The source is
   one single-specimen scRNA-seq reference (GSE229513,
   @sec-geo-design).
2. Choose that panel for the purpose: genes whose moments can be
   estimated in every type and that carry information about the
   proportions $\boldsymbol{p}$ (@sec-fs-scope).
3. Plug the moments into DeCovarT and deconvolve the bulk series
   (GSE229386) where a single-cell reference matches it: the
   standard-Wnt samples at 48 h, 72 h and 96 h.

The target is a covariance plug-in for the likelihood, not a
biologically interpretable gene regulatory network
([03-2, target](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-cov-target)).
Indices follow the article: gene $g=1,\ldots,G$, type
$j=1,\ldots,J$, bulk sample $i=1,\ldots,N$, cell $c$, with $C_j$ cells
of type $j$.

## Pipeline {#sec-pipeline}

@fig-pipeline lists the nine steps in the order the scripts run them.
Steps 2 to 5 are @sec-fs-scope; step 7 is @sec-cov-scope; step 8 is
[2.1, three regimes](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/02-1-single-cell-generative-optimisation.html#sec-three-regimes);
step 9 is @sec-deconv-models.

```{.tikz}
%%| label: fig-pipeline
%%| fig-cap: "Analysis pipeline, read left to right on each row. Row 1 builds the gene panel from the single-cell counts: quality control and a presence gate in every type (tier i), a count-model screen of the type effect ranked by deviance explained (tier ii), and a cross-platform filter (tier iii) fitted independently at each of the three matched pairs (single-cell 48 h, 72 h and 96 h against the standard-Wnt bulk at the same time). Row 2 estimates one covariance per type and time on the linear scale, with the tuning parameter of each estimator chosen by cross-validated held-out Gaussian log-likelihood, lifts the estimates to DeCovarT's moments and deconvolves the matched bulk at all three times. The dashed box is optional; it needs the covariances of step 7."
%%| filename: fig-pipeline
%%| alt: Two-row flowchart. Row one, left to right: 1 GSE229513 UMI counts and cell-type labels; 2 cell and gene quality control; 3 presence gate in every type; 4 omnibus deviance or quasi-likelihood screen, ranked by effect size; 5 bulk consistency filter fitted independently at 48, 72 and 96 hours, single-cell against standard-Wnt bulk at each matched time. An elbow arrow leads from step 5 to row two. Row two, left to right: 6 optional multivariate refinement by Fisher information or NSGA-II, drawn dashed with dashed arrows; 7 per type and time on the linear scale, shrinkage covariance as default, or graphical lasso, SILGGM or PLNnetwork, with lambda chosen by cross-validated held-out log-likelihood and nested cross-validation comparing the four; 8 lift to DeCovarT moments mu hat j and Sigma hat W j; 9 DeCovarT on the standard-Wnt bulk at 48, 72 and 96 hours, with a note that the early-Wnt bulk has no matched single-cell reference at any time.
```

## Reading guide {#sec-reading-guide}

Each chapter is the practice half of a vignette chapter. Read the
vignette for the model and the reasons; read the chapter for what is
run on Suppinger.

| Book chapter | What it runs | Theory (DeCovarT vignettes) |
|---|---|---|
| @sec-geo-design, Suppinger data | GEO objects, design, Seurat processing | [1.1 Generative model](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/01-1-population-generative-optimisation.html); [2.1 Three reference regimes](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/02-1-single-cell-generative-optimisation.html#sec-three-regimes) |
| @sec-fs-scope, Feature selection | tier (i) QC, markers and presence gate; tier (ii) four tests of the type effect and deviance rank; tier (iii) outliers and bulk tail filter | [3.1 Feature selection](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#wrn-fs-estimand) |
| @sec-cov-scope, Covariance estimation | four estimators, cross-validated tuning | [3.2 Covariance estimation](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-cov-target) |
| @sec-deconv-models, Comparators | DeCovarT, second-generation methods, NNLS and RLM baselines | [5.1 Review](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/05-1-review-distribution-aware.html); [2.1 From cells to reference moments](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/02-1-single-cell-generative-optimisation.html#sec-reference) |
| @sec-bio-deconv, Biological reading | early versus standard Wnt | none |
| @sec-sensitivity, Sensitivity | misspecification sweep, `scDesign3` calibration | [S5 Misspecification](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/S5-misspecification.html) |

: Book chapters and the vignette chapters that hold their theory. {#tbl-reading-guide}

Code in `R/` and `scripts/` is written to be run from the repository
root. Chunks marked `eval: false` show calls that have not been run in
the current state of the repository; the outputs they would produce are
listed as missing where it matters.
